THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 -4-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:11476  MFA No. 102342 of 2015  C/W MFA No. 102343 of 2015  MFA No. 102344 of 2015

ORAL JUDGMENT All these appeals are filed by the claimants/injured seeking enhancement of compensation being aggrieved by common judgment and award dated 25.02.2015 passed in MVC Nos.2154, 2155 & 2156 of 2013 on the file of learned Presiding Officer, Fast Track Court & Addl. MACT, Gokak1.
2.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned counsel Sri. Vijay K Naik for the appellants/injured in all these appeals submits that in MVC No.2154/2013, the injured was aged about 36 years, was working as Security Guard and earning Rs.10,000/- per month, however, the Tribunal has incorrectly assessed notional income of the injured at Rs.5,000/- per month, which is required to be re-assessed properly.
He submits that in MVC No.2155/2013, the injured is a daughter of the claimant in MVC No.2154/2013 and was aged about 4 years.
The Tribunal has awarded meager compensation under conventional heads.
Thus, seeks to enhance the same appropriately.

He further submits that in MVC No.2156/2013, the injured is a wife of the claimant in MVC No.2154/2013 and she has suffered fractural injuries,
however, the Tribunal did not consider the evidence of the claimant as 'Tribunal', for short NC:
2024:KHC-D:11476 well as doctor and thus, failed to award any compensation under the head of loss of future income due to disability.
He further submits that the award of compensation by the Tribunal is on the lower side and seeks to re-assess the same by considering her income on the higher side.
Thus, he seeks to allow all these appeals filed by the claimants/injured.

3. Per contra, learned counsel Sri. C.V. Angadi for the respondent/Insurer opposes the appeals and submits that since the Tribunal taking note of oral and documentary evidence on record has awarded just and proper compensation to all the claimants, the question of awarding higher compensation would not arise.

He further submits that insofar as disability assessed by the Tribunal in MVC No.2156/2013 is concerned, the evidence on record indicates that though the claimant has suffered fractures, those fractures are united, hence, question of awarding any compensation under the head of loss of future earnings due to disability would not arise.
Thus, he seeks to dismiss the appeals.
4. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record.

On 6.5.2013, the claimants/injured were proceeding on a motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-23/S-5617, at that time, Tempo Trax bearing registration No.KA-23/M-5783 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle resulted in injuries to all the claimants.

4 6.
Insofar as MVC No.2154/2013, the injured was aged about 36 years at the time of the accident and he was working as Security Guard and earning Rs.10,000/- per month.
However, no evidence is placed on record with regard to income of the appellant.
Hence, this Court would re-assess the income notionally at Rs.7,000/- per month placing reliance on notional income chart prepared by KSLSA.

Thus, loss of future earnings due to disability is reckoned as under:
Rs.7,000 x 12 x 16 x 35/100 = Rs.4,70,400/-
7.

Taking note of injuries suffered by the claimant and duration of treatment taken by him, this Court re-assesses the compensation as under:
 Pain and suffering Rs.1,00,000/-
 Medicine & Hospital charges Rs.1,10,830/-

Food, nourishment & attendant Rs. 15,000/-
 Loss of income during laid-up period Rs. 21,000/-

Loss of future income due to disability Rs.4,70,400/-
 Loss of amenities Rs. 40,000/-

------------------
 TOTAL Rs.7,57,230/-
 -----------------
 NC: 2024:KHC-D:11476 8. Insofar as MVC No.2155/2013 is concerned, the injured was aged about 4 years and sustained fractures in the road accident.

Taking note of fractures suffered by minor child, I am of the considered view that the Tribunal has committed an error in awarding meager compensation of Rs.65,000/-, which requires to be re-assessed as under:
 Pain and suffering Rs.40,000/-

Medicine & hospital charges Rs.14,000/-
 Food, nourishment & attendant Rs.15,000/-
 Loss of amenities Rs.30,000/-
 Loss of income during laid-up period Rs.15,000/-
 ----------------
9. Insofar as MVC No.2156/2013 is concerned, the claimant is the wife of claimant in MVC No.2154/2013, she was aged about 23 years and was earning substantial income from tailoring work.
However, no evidence is placed on record with regard to income of the injured.
Hence, this Court placing reliance on notional income chart prepared by KSLSA would re-assess the notional income of the injured at Rs.7,000/- per month.

Insofar as disability is concerned, medical evidence Girigouda @ Girish S/O Nagappa ... vs Basavaraj S/O Talappa Mahakali on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175891355/
5 on record indicates that the appellant has sustained fracture of lower end radius right, fracture of 4th and 5th metacarpal and scalp contusion right.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The medical evidence on record further NC:
2024:KHC-D:11476 indicates that those fractures are united, however, that should not be the only basis to deny disability to the claimant.

Taking note of said injuries suffered by the appellant, this Court is of the considered view that it would be just and appropriate to assess the disability at 5% for the purpose of determining the compensation.

Thus, the loss of future earnings due to disability is reckoned as under:
Rs.7,000 x 12 x 18 x 5/100 = Rs.75,600/-
10.

Taking note of nature of injuries suffered by the claimant and treatment provided to her, this Court re-assesses the entire compensation as under:
 Pain and suffering Rs.40,000/-
 Medicine & hospital charges Rs.20,375/-
 Food, nourishment, attendant Rs.20,000/-
 Loss of future earnings due to disability Rs.75,600/-
 Loss of income during laid-up period Rs.21,000/-
 Loss of amenities Rs.40,000/-
 ----------------

Total Rs.2,16,975/-
 Rounded off to Rs.2,17,000/-

11. In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER a) All the above appeals stand partly allowed.

b) The impugned common judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified holding that the claimant in MVC No.2154/2013 is entitled to NC: 2024:KHC-D:11476 total compensation of Rs.7,57,230/- as against Rs.6,11,830/- awarded by the Tribunal; the claimant in MVC No.2155/2013 is entitled to total compensation of Rs.1,14,000/- as against Rs.65,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal; and the claimant in MVC No.2156/2013 is entitled to total compensation of Rs.2,17,000/- as against Rs.1,00,375/- awarded by the Tribunal.

c) The enhanced compensation amount in all the above appeals shall carry interest at the rate of 6%
per annum from the date of petitions till realization.
d) The respondent No.3/Insurer shall deposit the enhanced compensation in all the appeals before the Tribunal within six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
